messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: P1 - runtime crashloop detected on pool 'serve-prod-us-east-1'. 40% of pods are CrashLoopBackOff. Auto-escalation to on-call.

sre-oncall: seeing segfaults in the runtime process in multiple pods across node-az1-07 and node-az1-09. Container logs show immediate SIGSEGV on startup. Attaching a sample from pod inference-runtime-7f8c9 (node node-az1-07).

sre-oncall: ```
[2026-03-15T10:12:03Z] runtime: segfault at 0 ip 0x7f4a2b1e0f3c sp 0x7ffd1a2bcd20 error 4
#0  0x7f4a2b1e0f3c in fused_kernel_apply+0x34
#1  0x7f4a2b1dff10 in start_inference_loop+0x120
#2  0x7f4a2b1a9a0 in main+0x60
Killed
```

sre-oncall: container id: docker://d3f9c4a2b6, image: redwood/runtime:2026.03.10-prod

maria: @sre-oncall thanks — looks like the segfault is inside the fused kernel path (TensorRT/Triton fused op). Can we collect core dumps and kernel logs from the affected nodes? Also need the full container stdout/stderr and the model variant ID for the failing requests.

sre-oncall: running remote commands now. setting kernel.core_pattern and enabling core dumps. grabbing dmesg and coredumpctl save for the runtime PID.

sre-oncall: ```
sudo sysctl -w kernel.core_pattern=/var/lib/core/core.%e.%p
sudo sysctl -w fs.suid_dumpable=1
mkdir -p /var/lib/core && chown 1000:1000 /var/lib/core
# on container host
dmesg | tail -n 80 > /tmp/node-az1-07-dmesg.log
```

carla: @maria @derek we should disable TRT fused kernels ASAP for the rollout. There is an env toggle REDWOOD_RUNTIME_DISABLE_FUSED=1 that forces fallback to safe kernels (slower but stable). If we flip that for the Deployment and roll one replica at a time, we can reduce customer impact quickly.

derek: cordoning node-az1-07 and node-az1-09 now to stop new pods scheduling. running drain with --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data. scaling up replacement capacity in us-east-1 pool by +3 nodes.

derek: ```
kubectl cordon node-az1-07
kubectl drain node-az1-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
kubectl cordon node-az1-09
kubectl drain node-az1-09 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
# spin up node pool:
cloudctl compute nodes create --region us-east-1 --count 3 --type g5.12x
```

customer-success: seeing ~6 customers with 5xx on generation calls, severity: P1 for two enterprise customers (requesting status). Tickets: INC-4512, INC-4513. They reported timeouts then 502s.

ben: can we quickly roll back runtime image to 2026.02.28 which was stable? That would remove the new fused-kernel runtime change. Alternatively toggle the env flag as carla suggested. Which is faster?

carla: toggling env is fastest — patch deployment to add REDWOOD_RUNTIME_DISABLE_FUSED=1 and set maxUnavailable:1 for rolling restart to keep capacity. I'll prepare the patch.

maria: please also capture /tmp/core.* files and upload to s3 bucket s3://redwood-incident-core-dumps/3351122334/ with node and pod metadata. We'll need to run gdb on the core to confirm the symbol.

sre-oncall: patch applied. rolling update started. patch snippet:```
kubectl -n prod set env deployment/inference-runtime REDWOOD_RUNTIME_DISABLE_FUSED=1
kubectl -n prod rollout status deployment/inference-runtime --watch
```

ops-bot: deploy-bot: rolling update triggered for deployment/inference-runtime by carla. 1/10 updated.

sre-oncall: after first updated pod came up, that instance handled traffic and did not segfault. We're seeing decrease in crashloop rate from 40% -> 15% in ~3 minutes.

carla: good — keep rolling. we'll keep an eye on latency regressions (expect ~10-25% slower per-token). Send customers a brief note via CS channel after mitigation.

derek: replacement nodes are up and autoscaler is adding 2 nodes; drained nodes have core dumps saved to /var/lib/core and uploaded.

maria: got the core dump, running quick gdb backtrace:```
$ gdb --batch -ex "thread apply all bt full" /opt/runtime/bin/runtime /var/lib/core/core.runtime.12345
#0  fused_kernel_apply (args=0x7f4a...) at fused_kernels.c:384
#1  0x00007f4a2b1dff10 in start_inference_loop at main.c:210
#2  0x00007f4a2b1a9a0 in main at main.c:78
```

maria: pointer deref null check missing in fused_kernel_apply when a particular plugin returns NULL on device memory allocate. Looks like a regression introduced in 2026.03.10. We should plan a rollback of that commit in the runtime repo after mitigation.

customer-success: UPDATE: major customer "AcmeAI" had degraded requests 10:12-10:28. CS has opened a bridge for their account team.

ben: recommend we continue the rollout but keep the toggle set cluster-wide until a safe runtime rebuild lands. Also add an integration test to catch NULL returns from plugin malloc paths.

sre-oncall: Incident status: mitigation in progress, crashloops reduced to 3 pods (from 40%). Traffic partially restored. No data loss. Tracking runbook steps in the incident doc: https://redwood.internal/incidents/3351122334 (create when we finish).

carla: request engineering timebox: rollback/rebuild window 4 hours. Maria will PR a patch to add null-check and fallback. QA will run on staging with fused disabled then re-enable for smoke.

maria: opened PR #4821 with fix and added test that simulates device malloc failure. CI running.

incident-bot: ALERT RESOLVED: crashloop rate back to baseline (0-1 pods) for pool 'serve-prod-us-east-1'. Monitoring in recovery window (30m).

sre-oncall: summary for postmortem: root cause - missing null-check in fused kernel path in runtime image 2026.03.10 causing SIGSEGV during device alloc failure; impact - partial outage for generation customers (several 5xx), mitigation - toggled REDWOOD_RUNTIME_DISABLE_FUSED=1 cluster-wide and rolled deployment, cordoned/drained affected nodes and collected core dumps, scaling added replacement nodes, fix PR #4821 opened; next steps - promote fix to canary with thorough smoke tests, add e2e to catch NULL plugin returns, customer outreach placeholder.

carla: assign owners: maria (fix + tests), ben (postmortem write), derek (node recovery + capacity), customer-success to notify affected accounts.

sre-oncall: I'll keep monitoring; will attach core dumps and logs to the incident doc and create the timeline. Good job team. :thumbsup:
